newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Vedrine says confident on euro.
newsitem.headline: France's Vedrine says confident on euro.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Hubert Vedrine has expressed confidence that the single European currency will be created as planned in 1999, saying it would help Europe become a true world power.

"I'm convinced that the euro will be created as foreseen by the (Maastricht) treaty, because it is of fundamental interest for all Europeans," Vedrine told the magazine Le Nouvel Observateur in an interview due to appear on Thursday.
"The military, economic and geopolitical consequences of giving up the plan for the single currency would all be worse than the difficulties in setting it up," he added.
Vedrine, who came to office last month in France's new Socialist-led government, also forecast deeper EU political cooperation. "Europe will become a political Europe," he said.
"(Europe) will become a true power, useful for the world, because we have to build a multi-polar world today between the different groups of countries or powers," he said.
He said that the single currency was overshadowing other projects, such as EU defence cooperation.

"Since European defence is not a priority for almost any of our partners for the time being, we must use different paths to advance, focusing notably on the creation of the single currency, all the while sticking to all other goals," he said.
